[**🇺🇸 EN**](README.en.md) · [🇨🇳 简中](README.zh-CN.md) · [🇯🇵 日本語](README.ja.md) · [🇰🇷 한국어](README.ko.md) · [🇫🇷 FR](README.fr.md) · [🇧🇷 PT-BR](README.pt-BR.md) · [🇹🇷 TR](README.tr.md) · [🇮🇩 ID](README.id.md) # AI Stickman Video Generator for Faceless YouTube Channels **Turn any idea into a high-quality stickman video with a consistent visual style.** [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/kaomei/stickman-video-director?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director/stargazers) ![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-16a34a?style=flat-square) Start with a topic, an article, or a link. Automatically create visuals, voiceover, captions, sound effects, and subtle animation, and get a complete stickman video. **Build a distinctive YouTube channel without ever appearing on camera.** An open-source collection of popular stickman animation styles from across the web, continually updated for **science and knowledge explainers, psychology and motivation, education and awareness, uplifting stories, trending stories, and more.**
Classic Black & White
 Modern Pop
Prehistoric Cave
 Cozy Storytelling
Historical Cartoon
 Minimal Hand-Drawn
**6 styles · 8 visual options · Tested examples · Free and open source** ⭐ **Star the project to keep up with new stickman styles as they arrive.** [Get started](#quick-start) · [A styles](#a-styles) · [B styles](#b-styles) · [FAQ](#faq)
## Two ways to make your video **Want control over every shot? Choose A · Director Mode. Want a finished long-form video without assembling every scene? Choose B · Autopilot Mode.** One project, two workflows. | |
A · Director Mode
|
B · Autopilot Mode
| |:---:|:---|:---| | **Approach** | **You control production; AI plans the shots.** Get storyboards and prompts, then generate clips and edit them yourself. | **Give it a topic or a brief; get a finished video.** Automate illustrations, voiceover, captions, subtle animation, and video assembly. | | **Length** | **Short-first**, typically 30 seconds–3 minutes. Longer videos can be built scene by scene. | **Long-form-first**, especially narrated videos of **10 minutes or more**. Also works for shorts and episodic stories. | | **Tools** | Plan with a Skill-compatible AI assistant, generate clips in **Google Flow** or a similar service, then edit in **CapCut** or your preferred editor. | Run in **Codex, Claude Code**, or another AI coding agent that can read and write files, call tools, and execute commands to connect generation with local rendering. | | **Visuals** | **Generated animated clips**, with character movement, camera direction, and interactions. | **Illustrated scenes with subtle animation**, using cuts, pans, and zooms to support the narration rather than generating a full-motion clip for every scene. | | **Output** | A director's treatment, storyboards, scene-by-scene video prompts, and sound design. | **A complete video file with voiceover, captions, and subtle animation.** | | **Start** |
Use Director Mode
|
Use Autopilot Mode
| Both workflows can start with **a topic, copy, or a complete script**. **A and B have separate style numbers, galleries, and visual assets; new styles and examples are added to their own series.** Choose the aspect ratio, narration language, and voice you need. The lengths above are recommendations, not limits. Autopilot Mode needs working image and voice generation services plus a local video-rendering environment. A standard chat window alone cannot replace that setup. The Skill is free and open source; connected services may charge separately. ## Get started Send the following to an AI assistant that supports Skills. After installation, it will explain **what each mode produces and how to begin**, with examples you can copy. ```text Install this Skill for me: https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director Once installed, read the installed SKILL.md right away. Explain what each mode produces, the tools it needs, and the workflow in plain language, with examples I can copy. Based on what I want to make, tell me what is missing and exactly what to do next. ``` ### A · Director Mode: scene-by-scene video prompts After installation, send this to your AI assistant and replace the placeholder with your topic: ```text Use Director Mode / mode A to turn the following topic, copy, or brief into a stickman video: [Enter a topic, paste your copy, or describe what you need] Requirements: landscape 16:9, A3 "Prehistoric Cave" style, starting with 30 seconds. Give me the director's treatment first. After I approve it, provide scene-by-scene video prompts. ``` **Workflow: share your topic and brief → develop the story script → optionally approve front, side, and back character views → generate detailed storyboard prompts → manually generate clips and edit the final video** The treatment covers the story structure, scene-by-scene narration, actions, camera direction, and sound design. Copy each prompt into [Google Flow](https://flow.google.com/) or another video generator, then add captions and finish the edit in CapCut or your preferred editor. For your first video, follow the [full production walkthrough](https://x.com/CrazyKaomei/status/2102311241046008268) (in Chinese). ### B · Autopilot Mode: from a brief to a long-form video After installing in Codex, Claude Code, or another environment with file access and command execution, try: ```text Use Autopilot Mode / mode B to turn the following topic, article, post, news item, or brief into a compelling YouTube video: [Paste content or a link, or describe what you want to promote] Requirements: 5–10 minutes, landscape 16:9, B1 "Minimal Hand-Drawn" style, with voiceover, captions, and sound effects. Check the image generation, voiceover, and video-rendering setup first. Then give me a script and a 20-second preview with sound. After I approve it, build the full video with visuals timed to the narration. Deliver a complete video file; I do not want to assemble scenes myself. ``` **Workflow: share a topic, content, or brief → approve the script → approve a 20-second preview with sound → automatically produce the full video → receive the finished video file** The AI assistant plans the scenes, generates the visuals and narration, adds captions and sound effects, and renders a complete video to the voiceover's timing. You approve the script and preview; you do not have to generate and assemble every scene yourself. On first use, it checks the required setup and walks you through anything missing. If a visual or voiceover section needs work, revise just that section and keep what you have already approved. ## A · Director Mode style gallery Styles are numbered A1, A2, A3… Each includes its own animated examples. ### A1: Classic Black & White Explain an idea with just a few lines. On a pure white or black canvas, characters, props, and a little accent color do the heavy lifting—ideal for brisk, clear explainers. - **Visual style**: simple round heads, line-drawn limbs, and consistent stroke widths, with occasional simple expressions. Up to three saturated accent colors signal emotion, risk, or action. Abstract ideas become visual metaphors: anxiety as a cage, attention as a progress bar. - **Best for**: science explainers, psychology, motivation, self-management, business breakdowns, and abstract concepts. - **Choose your look**: black characters on white feel clean and direct for teaching and everyday explainers. White characters on black create stronger contrast for suspense, conflict, and emotion. | A1.1 · Black on white | A1.2 · White on black | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Pure white canvas · Black characters | Pure black canvas · White characters | --- ### A2: Modern Pop A red beanie and yellow T-shirt give this character an instantly recognizable look. Explain a product in a clean tech setting, or follow the character into bedrooms, city streets, and the wilderness for a story with real ups and downs. - **Visual style**: a minimalist character with a consistent red beanie and yellow shirt, in two types of setting. Minimal Tech pairs white space and a faint grid with floating glass-like interfaces and cyan light. Colorful Story uses richer scenery, lighting, and depth to set the mood. - **Best for**: Minimal Tech suits AI tools, tech products, tutorials, and feature walkthroughs. Colorful Story works for personal growth, everyday life, adventure, and motivational stories. - **Choose your look**: explaining a tool or method? Pick Minimal Tech. Taking viewers through a character's experience? Pick Colorful Story. | A2.1 · Minimal Tech | A2.2 · Colorful Story | |:---:|:---:| | | | | White space · Faint grid · Cyan glow | Colorful scenes · Cinematic lighting · Story atmosphere | --- ### A3: Prehistoric Cave Take today's problems back to a world without phones or offices. Caves, animal skins, campfires, and exaggerated expressions turn the absurdities of work and human nature into short stories with a twist. - **Visual style**: bold hand-drawn strokes, solid white heads, dark limbs, animal-skin clothing, and earthy surroundings. Character interactions, reaction shots, and comic pauses drive the story. Design the cast for each story—different ages and genders are welcome; not every story needs the same face. - **Best for**: prehistoric what-ifs, workplace satire, observations on human nature, dark comedy, fables, and English-learning stories for children. - **Choose this when**: a small story needs an “aha” moment or an unexpected turn. Modern relationships transplanted into a prehistoric tribe make for jokes that feel both familiar and surprising. | Example 1: "How Did Humans Get Their First Job?" | Example 2: "The First Discovery of Fire" | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Prehistoric story · Workplace twist | Discovery of fire · Community creation | --- ### A4: Cozy Storytelling A mug too special to use. A message you feel you have to answer immediately. An afternoon finally kept for yourself. Simple characters inhabit colorful everyday settings, telling relatable stories through movement, expressions, and camera work. - **Visual style**: solid white round heads, slim bodies, fine dark limbs, and natural expressions in fully illustrated 2D environments. Wide shots establish the setting, close-ups capture hesitation or relief, and tracking shots follow the character forward. - **Best for**: relatable everyday stories, personal growth, relationships, heartwarming moments, habit-building, and English-learning content for children. - **Choose this when**: you want viewers to recognize themselves in a small moment. Adapt the colors and lighting to the theme, from warmth and comfort to anxiety, exhaustion, and starting over. | Example 1: Message anxiety on the commute | Example 2: Making time for yourself | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Subway station · Walking shots · Emotional close-ups | Outdoor café · Warm light · Everyday gestures | --- ### A5: Historical Cartoon Send stick figures into history: samurai on Edo streets, black cats in ancient Egyptian temples, soldiers in Roman camps. Period clothing, colorful settings, and playful contrasts make history easier to picture. - **Visual style**: solid white round heads, black oval eyes, bold clear outlines, and thin line-drawn limbs, paired with period clothing, soft cel shading, and colorful backgrounds. Change the costumes, buildings, props, and music for each place and era while keeping the same character drawing style. - **Best for**: world history, curious facts about civilizations, everyday life in the past, historical figures, and humorous history shorts. - **Choose this when**: you want to turn a fact into something a character actually experiences. Reactions and story twists help a small historical detail hold the viewer's attention. | Example 1: Edo Japan · A samurai's everyday life | Example 2: Ancient Egypt · Cats and mummies | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Edo streets · Samurai clothing · Everyday contrasts | Colorful temples · Black cat characters · History with a twist | Style and prompt contribution: [Lawal Ridwan / @leksautomate](https://github.com/leksautomate). --- ## B · Autopilot Mode style gallery Styles are numbered B1, B2, B3… Each has its own finished examples combining illustrated scenes with subtle animation, maintained separately from the A series. ### B1: Minimal Hand-Drawn Let the narration lead. Expressive stick figures, colorful hand-drawn props, and bold on-screen text make ideas, stories, and product benefits clear and engaging. - **Visual style**: near-white paper with a barely visible grid, black hand-drawn lines, and a few colorful props. Expressive faces, small animated details, flowing transitions, and sound effects keep the story moving. On-screen text highlights key ideas; captions follow the narration. - **Best for**: YouTube explainers, psychology and personal growth, workplace stories, educational videos, and product promotion. - **Choose this when**: you want a complete narrated, captioned video from a topic, copy, or story script. The visuals follow the voiceover's natural rhythm, making it a good fit for sustained explanations and long-form storytelling. Click a GIF to view or download the preview with sound.
Example 1: YouTube without showing your face Example 2: Why is nobody watching?
Hand-drawn characters · Key text · Subtle animation Bodi voiceover · Expressive faces · Subtle animation
--- ### B2: Coming soon… A style overview, dedicated examples, and usage prompts will be added here. ## Frequently asked questions ### Q1. Can I make a video without a script? Yes. Give the AI assistant a topic, an article, a link, or a brief, and it will shape that into a video script. You can also bring a finished script. Include your target audience, publishing platform, and intended length for a more focused result. ### Q2. Can Director Mode styles be fully automated? Why keep Director Mode? The A series currently has its own production workflows, but you can ask your AI assistant to combine your preferred A-series style with the B-series workflow for a DIY adaptation. Director Mode is retained primarily to keep video generation and experimentation costs under control. For a video over ten minutes long, one complete generation pass can cost **tens of US dollars**, and repeated attempts add to the bill. That's why Director Mode keeps generation and review scene by scene, followed by manual editing: you stay in control of every shot, check the results, and then decide whether to continue. ### Q3. How do I keep characters consistent in Director Mode? Ask your AI assistant: “First design a stick figure that fits my chosen style. Let me approve the front, side, and back views before writing the storyboard prompts.” This also works if you want a character of your own. Reuse approved character references when you have them; skip this optional step if you do not need a custom design. If your video tool supports reference images, **attach the approved character image to every clip you generate**. References supplement the existing storyboard prompts; they do not replace those prompts or change the selected style's rules. Check the finished clips for consistency. ### Q4. Do I have to use Codex? No. Director Mode works in AI assistants that support installing and using Skills. Autopilot Mode needs an environment such as Codex or Claude Code that can read and write files and execute commands, plus the required image generation, voiceover services, and local dependencies. ### Q5. How do I turn an article or reference into a more engaging video? Tell your AI assistant who you want to reach, what matters most, and what you want viewers to do afterward. It can develop the angle, opening hook, narrative progression, and call to action, then turn those into scenes. You can also share a reference video and say what you like about its pacing, delivery, or story structure. Learn from the approach while keeping your own perspective and wording. Verify historical, business, and scientific claims before publishing. ### Q6. Does it cost anything? The Skill is free and open source. Image generation, voiceover, and video generation services charge according to the platform and account plan you choose. A consumer subscription does not necessarily include API credits. ### Q7. Do I have to redo everything if a visual or voiceover is wrong? No. Approve the script and production plan first, then check a short preview for style, characters, voice, captions, and pacing before making the full video. If only one section needs work, revise that section and reuse the approved voiceover and assets to avoid unnecessary rework and generation costs. ### Q8. Can I publish on YouTube or use the videos commercially? The project uses the MIT license, which permits commercial use. Third-party images, music, sound effects, and voiceover services remain subject to their own license terms. YouTube monetization is subject to the platform's review and policies. ## More styles. More ways to create. ⭐ **Building a faceless YouTube channel and exploring content monetization?** Star this project for new stickman styles, video prompts, and automated workflows—so figuring out how to make the video stops holding your channel back. 🔔 **Follow [@CrazyKaomei](https://x.com/CrazyKaomei)** for faceless YouTube workflows and practical tools that connect scripting, voiceover, image generation, and editing. Spend less time on repetitive tasks and make consistent production more manageable as a solo creator, with more ideas on topics, channel growth, and monetization along the way. 🎨 **Planned styles**: illustrated storybooks, doodle fights, two-character sitcoms, card-based adventures, live-action/animation hybrids, and classroom explainers. 💬 **Ideas and submissions**: suggest a style, share your work, or report a problem by messaging [@CrazyKaomei](https://t.me/CrazyKaomei) on Telegram. For style requests, include a reference and the topic you want to cover. For submissions, include your video, the style used, and your creator link so your work can be showcased and credited.

[🇺🇸 EN](README.en.md) · [**🇨🇳 简中**](README.zh-CN.md) · [🇯🇵 日本語](README.ja.md) · [🇰🇷 한국어](README.ko.md) · [🇫🇷 FR](README.fr.md) · [🇧🇷 PT-BR](README.pt-BR.md) · [🇹🇷 TR](README.tr.md) · [🇮🇩 ID](README.id.md) # AI 火柴人视频生成器 **将任何想法变成一部高质量的、稳定画风火柴人视频。** [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/kaomei/stickman-video-director?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director/stargazers) ![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-16a34a?style=flat-square) 给一个话题、一篇文章或链接，自动制作画面、旁白、字幕、音效与微动画，交付完整火柴人视频。**不出镜，也能做出有辨识度的 YouTube 频道。** 汇总全网热门的火柴人画风，持续更新与开源——适用于 **知识科普、心理励志、教育宣传、情感治愈、流行故事等多赛道。**
经典黑白风
 现代潮酷风

 治愈故事风
历史卡通风
 极简手绘风
**6 大画风 · 8 种视觉方案 · 实测样片 · 免费开源** ⭐ **本系列持续更新，欢迎点个 Star，更多热门画风陆续上线。** [开始使用](#quick-start) · [A 画风](#a-styles) · [B 画风](#b-styles) · [常见问题](#faq)
## 两种视频制作模式 **想精细控制镜头，选 A · 导演模式；想做长片、不想逐段拼装，选 B · 全自动模式。** 同一个项目，两种制作方式。 | |
A · 导演模式
|
B · 全自动模式
| |:---:|:---|:---| | **特点** | **你来掌镜，AI 做导演**：生成分镜与提示词，由你控制片段生成和剪辑。 | **给出话题或需求，直接拿成片**：自动完成插画、配音、字幕、微动画与视频合成。 | | **时长** | **短片优先**，如 30 秒–3 分钟；也可逐段制作更长内容。 | **长片优先**，尤其适合 **10 分钟及以上**的旁白视频，也能做短片和连续故事短剧。 | | **工具** | 用支持 Skill 的 AI 助手做提案，再到 **Google Flow** 等平台生成片段，用**剪映**等工具剪辑。 | 在 **Codex、Claude Code** 等能读写文件、调用工具和执行命令的 AI 编程代理中运行，串起素材生成与本地合成。 | | **画面** | **逐段生成动画**：侧重角色动作、镜头调度与人物互动。 | **插画分镜＋微动画**：用切镜、推拉和平移配合旁白讲故事，不必逐段生成完整动作视频。 | | **产出** | 导演提案、分镜、逐段视频提示词与声音设计。 | **带配音、字幕与微动画的完整视频文件**。 | | **开始** |
使用导演模式
|
使用全自动模式
| 两种方式都可从**话题、文案或完整脚本**开始。**A、B 画风独立编号、分别展示，不共用画面；新画风与样片在各自系列下更新。** 画幅、旁白语言和音色按需选择。上面的时长是选型建议，不是硬性限制。 全自动模式需要可用的图像、配音等生成服务与本地视频合成环境；普通聊天窗口不能直接替代这套运行环境。Skill 免费开源，所接服务可能另行收费。 ## 开始使用 把下面这段发给支持 Skill 的 AI 助手。安装成功后，AI 助手会介绍**两种模式能做什么、如何开始**，并给出可以直接照着说的示例。 ```text 帮我安装这个 Skill： https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director 安装成功后，立即读取已安装的 SKILL.md， 用易懂的方式介绍两种模式的产出、所需工具和制作流程， 给我可以照着说的示例； 结合我的需求，告诉我还缺什么、下一步具体怎么做。 ``` ### A · 导演模式：逐段生成分镜提示词 安装后，把下面这段发给 AI 助手，换成自己的话题即可： ```text 使用导演模式/A模式，把下面的话题、文案或需求， 做成火柴人视频： [填写话题、粘贴文案，也可以直接描述需求] 需求：横屏 16:9，采用 A3「史前洞穴风」，先做 30 秒。 先给我导演提案，确认后再输出逐段视频提示词。 ``` **流程：给出话题和需求 → 生成故事脚本 → 按需确认人物三视图 → 生成详细分镜提示词 → 手动生成片段并剪辑成片** 提案包含故事结构、分段旁白、画面动作、镜头和声音设计。拿到提示词后，将它们逐条复制到 [Google Flow](https://flow.google.com/) 等视频生成工具，再用剪映等工具添加字幕、完成剪辑。 第一次做，可以跟着[完整制作教程](https://x.com/CrazyKaomei/status/2102311241046008268)跑一遍。 ### B · 全自动模式：一句话生成长片 在 Codex、Claude Code 等具备文件与命令执行能力的环境中，安装后这样说： ```text 使用全自动模式/B模式，把下面的话题、文章、帖子、新闻或具体需求， 做成在 YouTube 上有吸引力的视频： [粘贴内容或链接，也可以直接描述宣传需求] 需求：5～10 分钟，横屏 16:9，采用 B1「极简手绘风」，配上旁白、字幕和音效。 先检查生图、配音和视频合成配置，再给我脚本与 20 秒有声样片； 确认后，让画面跟随配音节奏自动完成整片，交付完整视频文件，不用我逐段拼装。 ``` **流程：给出话题、内容或需求 → 确认视频脚本 → 确认 20 秒有声样片 → 自动制作整片 → 拿到完整视频** AI 助手会根据内容设计分镜，生成画面与旁白，配好字幕和音效，再按配音节奏合成为完整视频。你主要负责确认脚本和样片，不用逐段生成、手动拼装。 首次使用会先检查所需配置，缺什么、怎么补都会逐步说明。画面或声音不满意，可以只调整对应片段，保留已经确认的部分。 ## A · 导演模式画风一览 按 A1、A2、A3…更新，每个画风下展示对应的动画样片。 ### A1：经典黑白风 用最少的线条，把一个概念讲清楚。纯白或纯黑的画布上，人物、道具和强调色承担主要信息，适合做节奏明快的知识解说。 - **画面特点**：简洁圆头、线条肢体与统一线宽，可偶尔加入简单表情；最多三种高饱和强调色，用来区分情绪、风险或行动。抽象内容可以变成具体画面，比如把焦虑画成牢笼，把注意力画成进度条。 - **适合内容**：科学常识、心理成长、励志、自我管理、商业拆解与概念解释。 - **怎么选**：白底黑火柴人清爽直观，适合教学和日常科普；黑底白火柴人对比更强，适合悬念、冲突和情绪表达。 | A1.1 · 白底黑火柴人 | A1.2 · 黑底白火柴人 | |:---:|:---:| | | | | 纯白画布 · 黑色人物 | 纯黑画布 · 白色人物 | --- ### A2：现代潮酷风 红色冷帽、黄色 T 恤，是这套画风最鲜明的角色标记。既可以在干净的科技空间里讲产品，也可以走进卧室、街道和荒野，演一段有起伏的故事。 -
